articles.description:
Description: Bug in SSH check mode with checkPeriod set to 0s.
What happened?
Check mode in Tailscale SSH forces an SSH client to periodically
re-authenticate when connecting to SSH servers. The period is configured via
the checkPeriod attribute in Tailscale ACLs, and defaults to 12 hours.
A bug in ACL parsing interpreted "checkPeriod": "0s" as unset, and used the
default period of 12 hours instead.
We deployed a fix for the bug in ACL parsing logic on 2024-04-23. SSH clients
in tailnets that set "checkPeriod": "0s" are now correctly prompted for
re-authentication on every connection.
Note that a special value "checkPeriod": "always" is the documented
recommended way to achieve this behavior.
We thank Finch for reporting this issue.
Who was affected?
17 tailnets use Tailscale SSH with "action": "check" and "checkPeriod": "0s". We notified security contacts for the affected tailnets about this bug.
What was the impact?
SSH clients in the affected tailnets were prompted to re-authenticate every 12
hours, instead of during each connection as intended by the tailnet
administrators.
What do I need to do?
No action is needed at this time.

Apr 21, 11:56 UTC
Update - Our Engineering team continues to work with upstream providers to resolve network connectivity issues that are occurring in multiple regions. As a result of multiple subsea fiber faults between Europe and Asia regions, the issues appear to be a direct consequence of congestion resulting in packet loss and increased latency connecting to the SGP1 region. Customers in the Asian region are having difficulty reaching DigitalOcean resources located in Amsterdam (AMS2, AMS3), London (LON1), and Frankfurt (FRA1).
We have no ETA for the upstream issues being restored but we will communicate any relevant information as we have it. We apologize for the inconvenience.
Apr 20, 16:20 UTC
Identified - We've confirmed the degraded network performance in our first update is due to a cable cut, which occurred at approximately 18:00 UTC, April 19. This cable is located just west of Singapore and impacts the cabling system connecting 17 countries from Singapore to Europe. Users can read more about the cable here: https://www.submarinenetworks.com/en/systems/asia-europe-africa/smw5

We continue to monitor this situation and progress of the repair. Our Engineering team will also continue to tune for performance and alternate routes where possible, until the issue is resolved.
If you have any questions, please open a Support ticket from within your account.
Apr 20, 12:10 UTC
Investigating - Due to multiple simultaneous subsea fibre cuts between Europe and Asia, we are observing degraded performance for European customers attempting to reach DigitalOcean resources hosted in our Singapore (SGP1) region, and Asian customers attempting to reach DigitalOcean resources hosted in our Amsterdam (AMS2, AMS3), London (LON1), and Frankfurt (FRA1) regions.
Engineers are attempting to improve performance where possible, but as this issue is largely out of our control we do not expect a substantial improvement in performance until one of the fibre cuts is repaired.
We apologize for any inconvenience.
articles.title: Subsea Fiber Faults Between Europe and Asia

Existing infrastructure (including Droplet and Droplet-based services networking) will continue running without issue. 
If the failover period lasts longer than expected, there may be customer impacts with associated services including: 
Droplet creates with a root password
Droplet root password resets 
MongoDB cluster creates 
Let’sEncrypt certificate creation (for Load Balancers and Spaces)
LoadBalancer creation with certificates
Spaces key creation
Marketplace (Add-Ons) will be unavailable for both vendors and users
App Platform builds and deploys may see latency 
Users will be unable to fetch CSV invoices 
Bulk actions in the Spaces UI

Incident began at 2024-04-22 11:10 and ended at 2024-04-23 16:50 (times are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC)).

Mini Incident Report

We apologize for the inconvenience this service disruption/outage may have caused. We would like to provide some information about this incident below. Please note, this information is based on our best knowledge at the time of posting and is subject to change as our investigation continues. If you have experienced impact outside of what is listed below, please reach out to Google Cloud Support using https://cloud.google.com/support or to Google Workspace Support using help article https://support.google.com/a/answer/1047213.

(All Times US/Pacific)

Incident Start: 22 April 2023 04:10

Incident End: 23 April 2023 09:50

Duration: 1 day, 5 hours, 40 mins

Affected Services and Features: Classroom

Regions/Zones: us-east1

Description:

Google Classroom experienced an increased error rate in Brazil (for the State of Paraná) due to hotspotting (overloading) in the product’s database for a duration of 1 day, 5 hours, 40 mins. From preliminary analysis, the root cause of hotspotting was a software bug, which we’ve fixed.

Customer Impact:

A subset of users in the state of Paraná, Brazil had encountered intermittent errors while accessing Google Classroom. To the best of our knowledge, no other customers were impacted.

Affected products: Classroom

Additionally, 0.15% of Webhook deliveries were degraded due to an unrelated spike in database latency in a single availability zone. SLOs for Actions were 90% during the incident, but this was not evenly distributed across customers. We statused green after a long stretch of recovered SLOs, starting at April 4th, 2024 00:35 UTC. We are investigating how we can improve resilience and our communication with our infrastructure provider, and how we can better handle ongoing incidents that are no longer impacting SLOs. Issue Summary: 
On April 18, 2024 from around 8:00 PM PDT to 10:28 PM PDT, users in non US English language settings were unable to create or update workflows.

We discovered that a data column had been omitted upon deployment. A fix was deployed for our users and normal service was resumed.
articles.title: Incident: Users see blank screen when attempting to create a workflow.

articles.description:
Issue summary:
On April 18, 2024 from around 9:00 AM PDT to 10:02 AM PDT, an automated monitoring system detected a high level of errors and backend database timeouts. We determined that some users may have experienced temporary service degradation and failed actions related to loading DMs and channels. Out of an abundance of caution, we began our incident response processes.

Our investigation traced this back to a backend service job that was causing the errors. As a remediation step, we manually ended the job which reduced the rate of errors back to normal and resolved the issue for all affected users.
articles.title: Incident: Some users may be experiencing general degradation issues that cause actions within Slack to fail.

articles.description:
Issue summary:
On April 8, 2024 from 2:32 PM PDT to 3:27 PM PDT, some users were unable to sign in, connect to Slack, access threads, run workflows, join huddles, or perform other activities. Apps and integrations may also have been impacted.

One of our databases failed and our automated recovery systems were not able to remedy the situation, requiring manual intervention. Our manual intervention restored normal functionality for most features, but it was not fully successful. There were some remaining issues with workflows that required further data recovery steps.

During this additional remediation work, we inadvertently caused a brief connectivity issue, preventing users from connecting to Slack for a very short period on April 9, 2024 at around 10:05 PM PDT. At 10:18 PM PDT our automated recovery systems successfully rectified the issue, ending connectivity problems for all customers.

We resumed our remediation work and concluded our data recovery efforts, resolving all remaining workflow issues. Additionally, this work included measures to prevent the same database failure from reoccurring in future.
articles.title: Outage: Trouble loading multiple features in Slack

articles.description:

One of our databases failed and our automated recovery systems were not able to remedy the situation, requiring manual intervention. Our manual intervention restored normal functionality for most features, but it was not fully successful. There were some remaining issues with workflows that required further data recovery steps.

We resumed our remediation work and concluded our data recovery efforts, resolving all remaining workflow issues. Additionally, this work included measures to prevent the same database failure from reoccurring in future.

articles.description:
Issue summary:
On April 12, 2024, from around 2:30 PM PDT until April 15, 2024, at 11:45 AM PDT, some users were unable to close a modal while in a huddle thread that was opened in a child window (a window popped open outside of the main Slack client).

This was commonly presented to users when they attempted to select an emoji from the emoji picker in a huddle thread but, we discovered this also occurred with other emoji picker modals that were open in a child window while using the desktop or browser versions of Slack.

We traced this issue back to a recent change we made to improve the modal navigation experience in Slack. We rolled back that change which resolved this issue for affected users.
articles.title: Incident: Modals opened in huddle threads cannot be closed

articles.description:
Issue Summary:

From Friday, April 5 at 11:48 AM PDT to Tuesday, April 9 at 3:37 PM PDT, users updated via our SCIM API were deactivated.

We traced this to a change that required API calls for this method to require a field not supplied by all identity providers. We rolled back this change and began remediation efforts to reactivate and restore users to their previous state. Though we previously stated some apps may need to be reactivated by Workspace Owners, we've since determined that all apps were reinstated through our remediation efforts.

We're analyzing data from this event to understand ways to mitigate similar issues that may occur in the future.
articles.title: Incident: Issues managing user accounts with the SCIM API

articles.description:
Issue Summary:

From Tuesday April 9 at 12:17 AM PDT to 7:21 AM PDT, users reported being unable to load the Workflow Builder page in Slack. 

We noticed an elevated error rate for API requests related to this page, and determined this was caused by a database issue that was in the process of being remediated. As remediation work continued, error rates subsided and the Workflow Builder page began to load as normal.

articles.description:
Issue Summary:
From April 4, 2024 at 12:30 PM PDT to April 4, 2024 at 10:20 PM PDT, some customers were receiving this error message when trying to rename a channel: “Oops/Whoops, something went wrong with renaming the channel. Please try again.”

We identified a code change which inadvertently altered the permission to edit channel. This resulted in this error being shown.

We rolled back this change, correcting the issue.

Impacted customers should no longer experience any further trouble after reloading their Slack.
To reload Slack use Command + Shift + R on Mac and Ctrl + Shift + R on Windows/Linux.
articles.title: Incident: Users receive an error message when attempting to rename a channel.

From April 1, 2024 at 5:13 PM PDT to April 2, 2024 at 12:36 PM PDT, some users experienced errors when submitting legacy workflows. 

A code change inadvertently introduced a logic error that sometimes resulted in an undefined workflow attribute. This caused affected workflows to crash, leading to an error message. 

We corrected the logic error, resolving the issue for all affected legacy workflows.

articles.description:

On April 2, 2024 from 2:50 PM PDT to 6:04 PM PDT, customers may have encountered missing messages in channels and conversations, as well as error messages in the Activity and Threads views. 

A code change inadvertently caused a rendering loop, preventing the Slack desktop client from correctly displaying some messages. We reverted the code change and rolled back to an earlier version, resolving the issue for all affected customers.

articles.description:
Issue summary:
From 3:41 PM PDT until 4:13 PM PDT on April 1st, 2024, some customers experienced problems with the Slack interface, including issues with text color and contrast.

We made a code change to improve some of our CSS styling. This change inadvertently caused a problem with some color and contrast variables in dark mode, resulting in the interface issues.

As an immediate mitigation step, we stopped the code change from rolling out any further. We then reverted to an earlier version, resolving the issues for all affected customers.
articles.title: Incident: Incorrect font color and unexpected UI elements

articles.description:
Issue summary:
From March 31, 2024 at 6:30 AM PDT to March 31, 2024 at 11:50 AM PDT, some customers were unable to create a channel with a workflow.

We identified a backend code change that inadvertently changed some data, causing the "Create a channel" workflow step to hang in the Workflow Builder.

We rolled back the change, correcting the issue. Impacted customers should no longer be experiencing any further issues.
articles.title: Incident: Workflows configured using the Create a channel step may encounter an error on channel creation

articles.description:
Issue summary:
On March 28, 2024 at 10:47 AM PDT until 11:20 AM PDT, a small number of users experienced trouble using workflows, connecting or signing into Slack, and creating accounts.

A recent change to a database service that's responsible for processing user activity in Slack had an influx of unexpected traffic. This traffic caused an increased number of error rates and failures which prevented users from accessing certain features.

When our internal health tools alerted us of the influx of errors, we paused any further code changes in an effort to improve database processing.

During our investigation, it was discovered that as a result of the unexpected traffic, the database service automatically timed out after about 30 minutes. This timeout allowed the database to return to normal and process new requests without causing errors.

We moved forward with a continued period of investigation and monitored to ensure impact did not reoccur.
articles.title: Incident: Trouble signing in and degraded workflows

articles.description:
Issue summary:
On March 27, 2024 from 8:13 AM PDT until 3:38 PM PDT, some users experienced errors when attempting to login, send messages, open channels, or threads.

We traced this issue back to a subset of errors that occurred within a set of cross-functional databases that are responsible for basic user features in Slack. As an immediate step to mitigate the issue, we automatically performed a restore of the backups of these affected databases.

Once the process of restoring these backups was completed, the databases began successfully processing user requests, fully restoring the functionality of the affected features. We are working to put safeguards in place to reduce the likelihood of this issue occurring again in the future.
articles.title: Incident: Issues loading Slack for less than 1% of customers

articles.description:
Issue Summary:
From Monday March 18, 2024 at 9:07 PM PDT to Tuesday March 19, 2024 until 12:06 AM PDT, some users saw blurry image previews.

A change was made to a backend service that's responsible for the handling of files in workspaces that have International Data Residency (IDR) enabled. This change inadvertently affected the ability for Slack to correctly generate previews for image files. On Tuesday March 19 around 12:06 AM PDT, we reverted the change to stop any new files to be loaded with blurry image previews. 

Thereafter, we conducted an in-depth investigation to find any images that were uploaded during the impacted duration to correct its image clearness. On Wednesday March 20, 12:50 PM PDT, all images were restored. 

Thank you for bearing with us while we worked through this case.
articles.title: Incident: Issues with file previews

articles.description:
Issue Summary:

From March 20, 2024 at 10:28 AM PDT to March 25, 2024 at 6:14 AM PDT, some customers in the US were unable to receive 2FA SMS codes.

This issue was traced to customers with a specific mobile carrier. We engaged with our upstream provider, who worked with the carrier to resolve the issue. 

Impacted customers should no longer be experiencing any trouble receiving 2FA SMS codes.

We apologize for any inconvenience caused and thank you for your patience.
articles.title: Incident: Some customers in US are not receiving 2FA SMS codes

articles.description:
Issue Summary:
From Monday March 25, 2024 at 3:30 PM PDT to Tuesday March 26, 2024 until 8:51 AM PDT, some users saw the error message REB686069408 when adding Google Sheets to their workflows.

This was traced to a backend change related to how Workflow Builder searches for a Google Sheet when using the Google Sheets workflow step, but the user interface was not receiving proper label values causing the error. 

We reverted the change as an initial attempt to fix, but learned this didn't resolve the issue as we continued to see incorrect value data.

We corrected the problematic piece of code that allowed for the Google Sheets step to properly search for the spreadsheet using the correct search value. This restored the workflow step to full functionality.
articles.title: Incident: Users receiving error when adding Google Sheets step to workflows.

articles.description:
Issue Summary:
On Monday March 25, 2024 at 6:00 AM PDT to around 8:00 AM PDT, some users did not receive two-factor authentication (2FA) codes via SMS and couldn't log into Slack.

We determined this was caused by an issue with an upstream 2FA provider. We monitored communications from the provider and confirmed Slack users could successfully sign in once the upstream issue was resolved.
articles.title: Incident: Users not receiving 2FA codes

Apr 16, 09:24 CEST
Scheduled - Dear customer,
 We are writing to inform you about an upcoming Scheduled infrastructure maintenance on 23.4.2024.  
This maintenance will take place between 10:00-11:00 AM CEST. 
How will this impact your workload? 
This maintenance, occurring at the database level and lasting up to one minute, is expected to cause delays in scenarios execution. This is because the webhooks will be affected and may be queued for a short period. 
We will inform you once the maintenance is completed. 
If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to reach out to our support team. 
Thank you very much. 
Kind regards, 
Your Make Team
